newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India auto stocks boost London GDRs.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India auto stocks boost London GDRs.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) benefitted from a rise in automobile stocks on the local market but London traders said the market was thin and reported little real buying interest.

"Indian auto stocks have pushed up locally and GDRs have moved up in line or a little bit ahead of the local stocks, but all we've seen are client sellers into the rally," said one dealer at a major UK firm. "We haven't seen any firm buying interest at all."
He pointed to Bajaj Autos, whose GDRs rose 6.5 percent to $29 today, after shooting up 20 percent over the past four days.
The Cazenove Indian GDR Index rose 2.35 points, or 3.71 percent, to 65.69 on Monday after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index jumped 77.50 points to a provisional 2,958.65.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index rose 2.07 percent to 58.66 by 1615 GMT, with the premium over the local market at 16.50 percent.

Traders said last week's announcement that India's Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) on companies might be removed or altered was fuelling the local market strength, but one said he doubted that any such change would take place.

"The government needs a minimum tax level out of these companies before it waives their expenses and our view is that it won't be abolished or changed," he said, adding such a move would incur problems for India for instance with the International Monetary Fund.
The local Indian markets have risen 7.0 percent since Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced on Thursday that the controversial MAT might be removed.
Like the auto sector, State Bank of India (SBI) and Telco GDRs were among the beneficiaries. Telco rose 73 cents to $9.73, while SBI climbed 81 cents to $15.88.
Meanwhile, traders said selling continued on the Korean market, with GDRs easing 2.02 percent to 59.39 on the HSBC James Capel GDR index.
One dealer said activity in Taiwanese GDRs remained light following the recent weakness in the U.S. stock market.
Capel's Taiwanese GDR index rose 0.73 percent to 94.23.
